classification.difficultyReason: Follow six different direction fields through two initial points, respecting stationary levels and changes in curvature.

content.prompt: For each slope field, draw solution curves through the two given points.

spec.description: Nine columns and nine rows of direction segments; no background grid. Horizontal segments at x=-4,0,4.
spec.mathematics: Direction depends only on x; negative for -4<x<0 and positive for 0<x<4.
spec.answerVisibility: Direction field and axes are permanent; solution curves are answer-only.

answer.short: i A trough with minimum at $(0,0)$. ii A vertically lower trough through $(2,0)$.
answer.worked: Plot both points. Follow the segments left and right, keeping each curve tangent to the field. Both curves have a minimum on $x=0$ and flatten towards $x=-4$ and $x=4$.

spec.description: Two smooth troughs with outward arrowheads.
Direction segments on x=-3 to 5 and y=-4 to 4; no background grid.
spec.mathematics: Slopes repeat vertically, are zero at x=1, positive to the left and negative to the right.

answer.short: i A downward-opening curve through $(0,0)$ with maximum near $(1,\tfrac12)$. ii A downward-opening curve with maximum at $(1,3)$.
answer.worked: Plot the points and follow the segments in both directions. Both curves rise for $x<1$, have horizontal tangents at $x=1$, then fall for $x>1$.

spec.description: Two downward-opening curves with arrows at their lower ends.
Nine-by-nine direction field; positive slopes repeat across horizontal rows and steepen away from the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Graphical reconstruction of the supplied directions; no equation is given in the source question.

answer.short: Two increasing curves through $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$, each least steep near $y=0$ and steeper above and below.
answer.worked: Plot the initial points. Follow the positive direction segments in both directions. Each curve flattens near the x-axis and becomes increasingly steep as $|y|$ increases.

spec.description: Two increasing curves with arrows at the lower and upper ends.
spec.mathematics: Graphical curves through the specified points.

spec.description: Horizontal-row direction field with zero slopes at y=-2 and y=2; all other shown segments incline positively.
spec.mathematics: Graphical reconstruction preserving the two equilibrium levels.

answer.short: Two increasing S-shaped curves through $(-2,0)$ and $(2,0)$, approaching $y=-2$ to the left and $y=2$ to the right.
answer.worked: Start at each initial point and follow the segments. Keep both curves between $y=-2$ and $y=2$, flattening towards these horizontal levels.

spec.description: Two increasing S-curves confined between the horizontal equilibrium levels.
Coordinate-dependent direction field with horizontal elements on the y-axis and vertical elements on the x-axis away from the origin.
spec.mathematics: Directions consistent with dy/dx=x/y; the origin has no direction segment.

answer.short: i An upper U-shaped curve with minimum at $(0,2)$. ii A left-opening curve with vertex at $(-2,0)$.
answer.worked: Through $(0,2)$, follow the field upwards on both sides of the y-axis. Through $(-2,0)$, draw the upper-left and lower-left arms, with a vertical tangent at the given point, as shown by the supplied field.

spec.description: Upper and left branches of rectangular hyperbolas with outward arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: Upper curve y²-x²=4; left-opening curve x²-y²=4, x≤-2.

spec.description: Direction field depending on both coordinates, with horizontal elements along the x-axis away from the origin.
spec.mathematics: Directions consistent with dy/dx=2y/x; omit undefined directions on x=0.

answer.short: i An upward-curving branch through $(1,1)$ on the right. ii An upward-curving branch through $(-2,1)$ on the left.
answer.worked: Plot $(1,1)$ and follow the positive slopes in the first quadrant. Plot $(-2,1)$ and follow the negative slopes in the second quadrant. Both branches approach the origin as they approach the y-axis; the second remains above the x-axis.

spec.description: Corrected branches through both stated initial points, replacing the incompatible lower source curve.
spec.mathematics: Right branch y=x² for x>0; left branch y=x²/4 for x<0. The origin is excluded.
